interface.name: wland_external_buffer_manager_v1

description.summary: wl_buffers that name content the embedder holds

interface.description:
A wland-private global: it makes wl_buffers out of an opaque 64-bit id instead of memory. No file descriptor and no pixels cross the connection; the compositor's embedder (the page hosting wland) turns the id into an image each time a surface commits the buffer. What an id means is agreed between the client and that embedder out of band (e.g. a renderer on the page that the client drives over its own channel).
The global is advertised only when the embedder said it resolves such ids, so its presence is the capability signal: a client that does not find it must use another buffer type (wl_shm).

entry.name: invalid_format
entry.summary: format is not one the manager takes

entry.name: y_invert
entry.summary: row 0 of the content is the bottom row

request.name: destroy
request.description: Buffers created through it are not affected.

request.name: create_buffer

description.summary: create a wl_buffer naming external content

request.description:
Create a wl_buffer of the given size whose content the embedder resolves from the id (id_hi is the upper 32 bits, id_lo the lower).
format is a DRM fourcc and must be one of ARGB8888, XRGB8888, ABGR8888 or XBGR8888 (invalid_format otherwise); X formats are opaque, the others carry pre-multiplied alpha. width and height must each be within 1..16384 (invalid_dimensions). flags may hold y_invert only (invalid_flags).
The buffer behaves like any wl_buffer. Content is taken at wl_surface.commit (copy on commit): the client must have the content complete at the embedder before it commits, must not change it until wl_buffer.release, and must damage what changed (a commit without damage shows nothing new). An id the embedder cannot resolve shows nothing new either; that is not an error.
An id must name the same content object for as long as a commit of any buffer made from it may be in flight; as no release follows the destruction of a busy buffer, a client should never give an id to another object.
